A_target.statement:
Let $C$ be a [[Definition:Circle|circle]] of [[Definition:Radius of Circle|radius]] $r$.
Then the [[Definition:Area|area]] enclosed by $C$ is:
:$\AA = \pi r^2$

B_source.statement:
Let $E$ be an [[Definition:Ellipse|ellipse]] with [[Definition:Semi-Major Axis|semi-major axis]] $a$ and [[Definition:Semi-Minor Axis|semi-minor axis]] $b$.
Then the [[Definition:Area|area]] enclosed by $E$ is:
:$\AA = \pi a b$

validity_conditions: A circle is precisely an ellipse whose two semi-axes are equal, so the specialization is an instantiation requiring no new argument.
Setting both semi-axes to r turns the product into r squared, giving the familiar formula.
The ellipse formula itself follows from the circle case by an area-scaling argument, so the two are equivalent rather than independent; the direction taken here is the instantiation.
proof_plan: A [[Definition:Circle|circle]] of radius $r$ is an ellipse with $a = b = r$.
